newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sri Lanka seeks Miri after term supply accord ends.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka seeks Miri after term supply accord ends.

text.p: Sri Lanka has used up its contractual volume of Miri crude from Malaysia's Petronas for 1996 and is seeking to top up its storage tanks through a spot tender, a refinery official said on Friday.
As reported, state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) tendered earlier this week to buy 450,000 barrels of light sweet Malaysian Miri crude for December 10-12 delivery to Colombo.
The tender closes on November 13 and offers should be valid for two days.

A refinery official said the delivery would go into a 60,000-tonne storage for Miri crude. The refinery uses Miri to blend with Middle East crude supplies for running in its 60,000-barrel-per-day Sapugaskanda refinery.
The official said the cargo would tide the refinery over for the remainder of the year. He said he expected another term agreement to be finalised to cover next year's requirements.
"Once we receive this Miri cargo, it will be sufficient for this year," he said.
Malaysian state-oil group Petronas has a one-year contract to supply 300,000 tonnes of Miri crude for the refinery. The final shipment of 450,000 barrels was discharged at the refinery two weeks ago.
Traders said CPC might only find a few offers of Miri, which is rarely traded on the spot market.
December prices on a free-on-board (fob) Malaysia basis were assessed on Friday at $24.75 and at a $1.10-premium to published quotes.
